feasibility.verdict: Partially feasible: ELM (single-column) can simulate agricultural nitrogen cycling and vertical nitrate leaching below the root zone; ELM-PFLOTRAN coupling can add 1-D vertical reactive transport of nitrate through the vadose/saturated column. However, lateral saturated groundwater transport from fields to specific drinking-water wells and true well 'arrival concentrations' require a 3-D groundwater flow-and-transport model (well-field geometry, pumping, aquifer heterogeneity) that a single-column configuration cannot represent.
answerable: Field-scale fertilizer N inputs, plant uptake, mineralization/nitrification/denitrification, and nitrate leaching flux below the root zone (kg N ha-1 yr-1)
Vertical nitrate concentration profiles and downward leaching to the water table via ELM-PFLOTRAN 1-D reactive transport
Interannual and seasonal variability of leaching driven by 1980-2018 meteorology and land-use (corn/soy) management
not_answerable: Lateral groundwater transport from fields to a specific well location (needs 3-D flow/transport)
Actual nitrate arrival concentration and travel time at a pumping drinking-water well (needs aquifer model with well capture zone)
Mixing/dilution in the regional aquifer and dispersion along flow paths
Well-specific pumping-induced drawdown and capture-zone dynamics

parsed.n_justification: Three single columns capture the dominant nitrate-source and land-management gradients of the Upper Iowa basin (HUC 07060002): an upland well-drained loamy tile-drained corn-soy field, a low-terrace poorly drained silty clay loam field, and a near-stream sandy-loam recharge zone that most directly connects to shallow drinking-water wells. This spans the leaching-controlling variability (texture, drainage, position) without implying lateral connectivity the model cannot resolve.
requires_capabilities: ELM active biogeochemistry (CN/CNP) with agricultural crop and fertilizer management (mksurfdata crop PFTs, prescribed fertilizer)
ELM-PFLOTRAN coupling for 1-D vertical reactive nitrate transport through the vadose and saturated zone
PFLOTRAN nitrification/denitrification reaction network configured to match ELM soil N pools
GSWP3 or Daymet meteorological forcing (1980-2018) for the domain
External well nitrate records for benchmarking leaching output (not directly comparable without a groundwater model)
3-D groundwater flow-and-transport model (e.g., standalone PFLOTRAN 3-D or MODFLOW-MT3D) to translate leaching flux into well arrival concentrations — OUTSIDE single-column scope
assumptions: Fertilizer application follows standard Midwest corn-soybean rotation rates unless site-specific rates are supplied
Land use is agricultural row crop for all three columns, consistent with the single 'land use' driver available
First few simulation years serve as spin-up; an additional accelerated-decomposition BGC spin-up is run before the transient period
Nitrate leaching below the root zone is reported as a flux boundary; conversion to well concentration requires downstream 3-D groundwater modeling not performed here
Aquifer/well geometry, pumping rates, and dispersivity are unknown and therefore not represented
Drinking-water wells tap the shallow alluvial/karst aquifer hydraulically connected to the near-stream recharge zone (used only to select the most relevant recharge column, not to compute transport)
